concept: 可替换的模型与执行基座
prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: wide 16:9 editorial illustration for a technology research article about composable embedded AI agents. Theme: interchangeable LLM providers and execution harnesses sharing one stable interface foundation. Visual metaphor: a precise modular computing assembly in an exploded horizontal arrangement. Three unbranded rectangular compute cartridges with clearly different circuit-board geometries hover just above a common pale ceramic backplane; beneath them one graphite adapter frame with matching connector sockets; on the right a few clear glass component planes emerge from the common backplane, containing sparse geometric diagrams, bars and nodes without any letters. The physical fit between replaceable modules, adapter frame, and one shared foundation must be immediately readable. Materials: sharply cut black-and-white macro photographs of modern silicon chips, PCB edge connectors, graphite heat sinks and thin optical glass; combine with exact flat modernist geometric fields and fine technical linework. Composition: generous off-white negative space, asymmetric balanced arrangement, strong large silhouettes, mostly frontal three-quarter technical photography, no crowded room or computer desk. Style: conceptual editorial collage, scientific photomontage, contemporary technology research publication, restrained archival-photo treatment of MODERN hardware, subtle halftone and very light ink texture, clean precise edges. Palette: warm white and charcoal with one muted cobalt-blue plane and one small desaturated olive shape; avoid sepia, antique brass, yellow cast and heavy weathering. Constraints: no typography, no letters, no numerals, no logos, no watermark, no branded chip labels, no literal screenshot, no humanoid robot, no brain, no neon cyberpunk, no random vintage printing machinery. Technology should be evident in the silicon, connectors and modular hardware. This is an original AI-created conceptual illustration, not a historical document.

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: wide 16:9 editorial illustration for a technology research article, same coherent series as an off-white, charcoal and cobalt modular-computing collage. Theme: an agent's continuous event stream becomes a live interactive interface, with user input feeding back to the running task. Visual metaphor: at the left, a carefully cut macro photograph of a modern fiber-optic ribbon cable and a small unbranded optical transceiver. A sparse procession of dark signal beads and short cyan-cobalt segments runs along a clean curved technical path through a single translucent rectangular decoding gate at center. To the right this path unfolds into three floating optical-glass interface planes, one with a simple line plot, one with a sparse slider and choices represented by circles, one with a clean two-column data arrangement represented only by lines and dots. A single fine return path arcs from the nearest control plane back toward the transceiver, making a quiet feedback loop. Composition: horizontal left-to-right movement, deliberate generous off-white whitespace, only a handful of strong large elements, asymmetric modernist print composition; not a triptych, not a busy dashboard. Materials: contemporary black-and-white technology macro photographic cutouts, translucent optical glass, precise scientific line drawing, a flat desaturated cobalt area and small muted olive accent, subtle sparse halftone texture and paper grain. Style: conceptual editorial collage, scientific photomontage, contemporary research publication, clean tactile materials and sharply readable silhouettes, not glossy futuristic advertising. Palette: predominantly warm white, charcoal and subtle cool grey; controlled cobalt-blue accents indicate the signal, no neon glow. Constraints: absolutely no letters, words, numerals, captions, logos or watermarks; no code screenshot, no computer monitor, no brain, no robot, no antique machinery, no random retro objects, no tangled wiring, no decorative hologram clutter. The signal becoming interface and the return interaction should be readable without labels.

concept: 组件扩展与局部状态更新
prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: wide 16:9 editorial illustration for the same contemporary AI technology research article series. Theme: extensible UI components and precise real-time state updates, where one part changes while the rest remains connected. Visual metaphor: a carefully composed array of six discrete clear and frosted glass interface tiles mounted above a large cropped black-and-white silicon wafer. Each tile carries a different sparse geometric visual grammar, such as a few data dots, one line chart, a slider track, a simple modular grid or a short stack of rules, WITHOUT text. Five tiles remain seated and neutral. One cobalt-tinted tile is raised slightly out of its exact matching slot, revealing a clean connector footprint beneath and a fine continued state trace through the array. One new small neutral tile approaching an empty edge connector indicates extension without replacing the entire system. Composition: clear top-down three-quarter macro perspective, large balanced shapes, asymmetric offset array mainly in the center and right, generous warm-white negative space on the left, the silicon wafer is a photographic grounding element rather than a decorative circuit background. No repeated compute boards or fiber cables from other images. Materials: monochrome macro photography of modern silicon and microfabrication, precisely cut optical-glass shapes, subtle halftone print grain, a small flat muted olive field underneath the far edge, fine controlled technical trace lines. Style: conceptual editorial collage, scientific photomontage, modernist research-publication composition, restrained tactile print texture, accurate-looking contemporary tech materials. Palette: off-white paper, charcoal and translucent grey; one desaturated cobalt-blue updated tile, tiny olive accent. Constraints: no letters, no numbers, no labels, no logos, no watermarks, no real UI screenshot, no holographic clutter, no neon cyberpunk, no humanoid robot, no brain, no antique instruments, no brass machinery, no cables everywhere. Make the independent tile, stable shared connections and local update immediately understandable. This is conceptual editorial artwork, not a literal engineering schematic.
